April closes with a familiar pattern: technology stocks moving higher while digital assets take a pause. As the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.58% in the last session, both Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen minor pullbacks over the past week, with the VIX indicating elevated caution. In the stock markets, major tech earnings have exceeded expectations, pushing the Nasdaq 100 higher and supporting a broader risk-on tone that can extend into digital assets. This is reflected in Bitcoin dominance, which has risen to around 58.0% of the total crypto market capitalisation. In a market defined by mixed signals, Nasdaq strength contrasts with Bitcoin and Ethereum consolidation, all while the VIX remains elevated, the structure of your portfolio becomes key.

## Carnegie Investment Counsel Blog. Tax season is coming to a close, earnings season is set to begin, and renewed geopolitical tensions are influencing markets — most visibly through energy prices. While these may appear to be separate headlines, they are interconnected parts of a broader environment the market is working to process. This is typical for this time of year: periods of short-term uncertainty often emerge even as the underlying, longer-term foundation remains more stable than the headlines suggest. ## What We’re Watching in April. April naturally puts taxes front and center, but beyond the filing deadline, it’s also a good moment to revisit the basics. These decisions don’t feel urgent in the moment, yet they tend to be the ones that compound most effectively over the long run. It’s a quieter force, but an important one, and a reminder that not all of the underlying trends are working against the market.
